My new setup: Python/FastAPI backend, plain HTML/JS frontend, Postgres on Supabase, deployed on Railway. Simple enough for me to maintain on my own and share access with my family, all without being locked into SAAS walled gardens.

Paper #1: phones hurt cognition.
Paper #2: phones help cognition.

Both published, but no recon
tweets.body:
This basically sums up everything that's wrong with psychology:

Paper #1: phones hurt cognition.
Paper #2: phones help cognition.

Both published, but no reconciliation, no net contribution to understanding how we operate.

**50%** of all psychology studies do not replicate. It's bonkers.

I’m putting together a small research/work circle called PIONEERS, based in London, to dig into this properly, exploring what robust behavioural science should and could actually look like in the new AI age.

If you care about fixing this, DM me.

tweets.title: When exiting to Facebook in 2020, we had a 'signing party' for our employees, both past and present. I gave a rousing speech similar to those I had given every
tweets.body:
When exiting to Facebook in 2020, we had a 'signing party' for our employees, both past and present. I gave a rousing speech similar to those I had given every week for company all-hands, then when everybody was upstairs celebrating, I went downstairs, called our lead investor and wept.

I'm conscious of bemoaning problems of the privileged, but the identity of founders and their startup/team is so tightly coupled, it felt like losing a big part of oneself.

The first 6 months at FB was a fog, after which I set myself a new year's resolution to 'find my value' in the company, which I'm happy to say I found.

Now five years on and having recently departed Meta, I'm looking forward to resetting, navigating the maze, and creating value once again.
